tasks.title: Keystone Species Effects
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a biology class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker talk about arches in architecture?

options.A: To point out a similarity to rock arches in nature
options.B: To help illustrate an important concept
options.C: To argue against a common comparison
options.D: To show a difference between life science and technology fields

questions.stem: According to the talk, what is a keystone species?

options.A: A species that is necessary to maintain balance in an ecosystem
options.B: A species that has no predators within an ecosystem
options.C: A species that is too numerous for a healthy ecosystem
options.D: A species that is negatively affected by environmental changes

questions.stem: In the early 20th century, what happened to the wolves in Yellowstone National Park?

options.A: Their population increased dramatically when their prey population increased.
options.C: They were eliminated over farming and safety concerns.
options.D: Their population decreased significantly because of disease.

questions.stem: How did an increasing elk population affect the Yellowstone ecosystem?

options.A: Many species were negatively affected due to the elk's diet.
options.B: Various animals that prey on elk were attracted to the area.
options.C: Some areas developed an overgrowth of plants while others had too little vegetation.
options.D: The population and range of the wolves also increased.

tasks.title: Dark Stores and Retail Tradeoffs
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a business class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What aspect of dark stores does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: Their influence on the retail market and society
options.D: Their role in the history of warehouse development

questions.stem: According to the talk, why can dark stores offer lower prices?

options.A: Because they sell large quantities of goods
options.B: Because they are not focused on making a profit
options.C: Because they obtain less expensive products
options.D: Because they have lower overhead expenses

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention grocery delivery?

options.A: To illustrate how dark stores compete with traditional supermarkets
options.B: To compare delivery speeds in urban and nonurban environments
options.C: To suggest that dark stores mainly sell perishable items
options.D: To explain why grocery delivery has become less popular

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about dark stores and employment?

options.A: Many temporary employees are needed to set dark stores up.
options.B: Employees in dark stores need to be comfortable with technology.
options.C: Dark stores do not need many in-store workers.
options.D: Dark stores are able to pay their employees more.

tasks.title: Sustainable Adobe Construction
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an architecture class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: The renewed use of an old construction material
options.B: Recent advances in sustainable building materials
options.C: The challenges faced by ancient adobe brick builders

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about a new building in Amsterdam?

options.A: It was inspired by adobe construction.
options.B: It is made from very common natural materials.
options.C: It removes carbon from the atmosphere.
options.D: It involves technology that improves insulation.

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about conditions in places in the southwestern United States?

options.A: Major changes in temperature occur there.
options.B: Air there has recently become polluted.
options.C: Not all materials for adobe production are available there.
options.D: More clay for construction is available there than in other places.

questions.stem: What does the speaker emphasize about transportation for construction projects?

options.A: Calculating its costs takes a long time.
options.B: It requires special technology when concrete is used.
options.C: The need for it depends mostly on the location of the project.
options.D: Using adobe bricks helps reduce the need for it.

tasks.title: Poverty Point Engineering and Trade Networks
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class. Then answer the questions.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the lecture?

options.A: To describe how trade networks developed among ancient societies in North America
options.B: To highlight an ancient site that required large-scale planning
options.C: To explain the role of metal tools in ancient construction
options.D: To compare different types of prehistoric earthen mounds

questions.stem: What aspect of the earthen mounds is most impressive to the speaker?

options.D: The knowledge required to build them

questions.stem: What does the speaker emphasize about how the structures at Poverty Point were built?

options.A: They required advanced knowledge of metal technology.
options.B: They depended on materials from distant regions.
options.C: They involved a large amount of manual effort.
options.D: They were completed in a short period of time.

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about the Mississippi River?

options.A: It contained resources that were used for construction.
options.B: It was the main source of food for people at Poverty Point.
options.C: It connected people at Poverty Point to distant areas.
options.D: It enabled people from Poverty Point to relocate to other regions.
